long_biography.plain_text:
Florida governors twice tapped Albert R. Maury for public governance: first as an FIU trustee, then for a four-year wildlife-commission term. At FIU he became the first undergraduate alumnus on the governing board and served as chairman after leading its finance and audit work. These appointments extended a South Florida civic record that also included ageing and children's nonprofits.

Maury's institutional experience grew from three decades in managed healthcare. After early work at Physicians Corporation of America and Neighborhood Health Partnership, he moved to the newly opened Leon enterprise. There he designed financial and administrative systems, ran its Medicare Advantage insurer and ultimately took charge of the medical-centre network. Maury also served as a company director and held a six-percent stake alongside his operating duties; he is founder Benjamín León Jr.'s son-in-law.
